title: Church Discipline
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Church discipline is the loving and biblical correction of sin within the church for the honor of Christ, the protection of the body, and the repentance and restoration of the sinner. It is not punishment for control, but correction under the authority of Christ.
summary: Church discipline is the loving and biblical correction of sin within the church for the honor of Christ, the protection of the body, and the repentance and restoration of the sinner. It is not punishment for control, but correction under the authority of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ loves His church too much to leave sin unaddressed. He calls His people to holiness, repentance, forgiveness, and restoration, and He gives the church instructions for correcting sin with truth and love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church discipline begins with the holiness of Christ and His love for His people. Sin is never harmless in the body of Christ. It damages the sinner, harms others, weakens witness, and dishonors the Lord.

Jesus gives a process for addressing sin that begins personally and privately when possible. The goal is not embarrassment, control, or revenge, but winning the brother or sister back. Discipline should move with patience, truth, humility, and appropriate seriousness.

Scripture also shows that persistent, public, unrepentant sin may require public correction and even removal from fellowship. This is not because the church is sinless, but because Christ calls His church to holiness and repentance.

Discipline must always be tied to the hope of restoration where repentance is present. The church must not ignore sin, but neither should it crush the repentant. Biblical discipline protects the flock, calls sinners back, and displays the seriousness and mercy of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many churches either avoid correction entirely or misuse correction harshly. Avoidance allows sin to spread and people to be harmed. Misuse creates fear, shame, control, and spiritual abuse. Scripture gives a better way: truth joined with humility, holiness joined with mercy, correction aimed toward restoration.

This doctrine is especially important for people who have been wounded by church failure. Biblical discipline is not a weapon for leaders to protect themselves. It is Christ’s means of protecting His people, calling sinners to repentance, and preserving the church’s witness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive correction with humility when Scripture exposes sin, and give correction carefully when love requires it. Do not ignore destructive sin, gossip about it, or weaponize it. Follow Christ’s pattern with truth, patience, prayer, proper order, and a desire for repentance and restoration. When someone repents, be ready to forgive, comfort, and reaffirm love.
